input_candidates.spec:
The required synthesizable top module is adaptive_aero_control_top. Do not substitute a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module as the design top. The top must implement the selected Physical AI application contract, external model request/response transport, validation, safety, timeout, fallback, and bounded actuator-command behavior.

EXTERNAL MODEL TRANSPORT DIRECTION CONTRACT (mandatory; this takes precedence over ambiguous ingress/egress wording in upstream prose): the RTL emits model-request valid/data as outputs and receives model-request ready as an input. The RTL receives model-response valid/data as inputs and emits model-response ready as an output. Apply this rule by data flow even when application-specific ports use cmd_*, req_*, rsp_*, or response_* names. A top-level output must have a real RTL driver; never connect a required top-level output only to a child input.
Implement a synthesizable FPGA top module named adaptive_aero_control_top with a compact 64-bit register-mapped control/status interface and bounded 64-bit request/response transport. The RTL shall not implement the DoMINO surrogate itself; it shall only package requests, validate responses, manage timeouts, and generate safe actuator commands.

Top-level ports shall include clk, rst_n, a 64-bit memory-mapped register window interface, a 64-bit valid/ready request channel to the external CPU/GPU surrogate service, a 64-bit valid/ready response channel from that service, a 32-bit actuator command output with valid and mode, and a 1-bit interrupt/status output. No tensor, geometry array, or flow-field bus may appear at the top level.

The register window shall provide at minimum: control enable, soft reset, request sequence number, request launch bit, timeout threshold, maximum/minimum actuator command limits, fallback command value, fault clear, status readback, and optional operating-point fields sufficient to describe stream velocity within the supported envelope. The design may use small flip-flop-based control registers and counters only. Bulk geometry or payload storage shall remain outside RTL in firmware/software.

The request_packager shall create a single outbound transaction on surrogate_req when a launch bit is asserted and the module is enabled. Each transaction shall include a monotonically incrementing sequence number, a request type tag, and compact context fields sufficient for the external service to reconstruct the requested operating point. The packager shall hold the request valid until ready is observed and shall not issue a new request while one is outstanding unless explicitly configured for pipelined operation via a small outstanding counter.

The response_validator shall accept only responses that match the expected sequence number or token, are marked valid, arrive before the programmable timeout expires, and pass range checks. If the response contains an actuator command, the command shall be interpreted only as a bounded control suggestion; the command_limiter shall clamp it to the configured min/max bounds and may apply a programmable step limit per update. Invalid, malformed, or stale responses shall be discarded and shall not update the actuator output.

The timeout_stale_monitor shall maintain a cycle counter for each outstanding request or for the single current request in the non-pipelined configuration. If the response does not arrive before the configured timeout threshold, the module shall set a timeout fault, increment a timeout counter, and enter safe fallback. The monitor shall also detect stale-data conditions when a response sequence is older than the active request, when the host firmware reports session rollover, or when the request age exceeds a freshness threshold.

The safe_fallback_controller shall select a deterministic safe command when the system is disabled, in reset, awaiting response beyond timeout, or upon any validation failure. Safe fallback shall be programmable but default to a conservative aerodynamic position or hold-last-safe behavior. On fault entry, the controller shall assert a fault status bit and provide a stable fallback actuator command until cleared by firmware or until a valid new command is accepted.

The actuator_output_stage shall register the final command, drive actuator_cmd[31:0] and actuator_valid, and encode mode to indicate normal closed-loop update, fallback hold, or fault-safe state. The output stage shall never emit an unclamped command. If slew limiting is implemented, it shall constrain command delta per update using a small arithmetic comparator/subtractor datapath.

The telemetry_status block shall expose the current state machine state, busy/idle, outstanding request count, last accepted sequence number, timeout fault, stale fault, protocol fault, clamp-active flag, fallback-active flag, and a response counter. The status IRQ shall pulse or level-assert on response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry according to a register bit.

All logic shall be fully synchronous to clk with active-low rst_n. The design shall be synthesizable for FPGA implementation and shall not infer ASIC-only macros. For FPGA storage, use standard FPGA-flavored register logic or the target toolchain's BRAM abstraction only if a deeper queue is later required; do not use Sky130 hard macros in this FPGA path.

The implementation shall support the application envelope of 20 to 55 m/s and shall permit the host to program the representative operating point of 38.89 m/s with DrivAerML reference geometry identifiers. However, the hardware shall remain agnostic to raw geometry payload size and shall only transport compact identifiers and control metadata.

Reset behavior: after rst_n deassertion, clear outstanding requests, clear valid outputs, set safe fallback active, initialize command output to the fallback value, clear fault latches unless a sticky-fault mode register requests retention, and set the module idle. All counters and sequence numbers shall initialize deterministically.

Handshake behavior: surrogate_req.valid shall remain asserted until surrogate_req.ready is seen. surrogate_rsp.ready may be asserted whenever the module is able to accept a response. No combinational loop shall exist between request and response handshakes. The register interface shall return error for unsupported addresses.

This RTL shall be suitable for an Arch2RTL workflow that emits synthesizable control logic around an externally executed physics surrogate, with emphasis on validation, bounded I/O, safety, and deterministic fallback.
FPGA MEMORY CONTRACT (mandatory): describe bulk payload/history/FIFO storage through a technology-neutral memory wrapper that the FPGA flow can map to native block RAM; do not flatten it into registers.
